args.body:
PLAN OF REORGANIZATION — DEVIATION REPORT
Committee Redline vs. Debtor’s Original Plan
Confidential — Attorney Work Product

Matter: Bankruptcy Restructuring — Analyze Counterparty Markup of Plan of Reorganization
Source materials (Matter File 4): Deal materials — bankruptcy-restructuring analyze: Analyze Counterparty Markup of Plan of Reorgan
Referenced working set (per engagement instruction): committee redlined plan; debtor’s original plan; valuation summary; transmittal email; disclosure statement excerpts
Output file: plan-deviation-report.docx
Practice area: Bankruptcy restructuring


I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

This report compares the Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors’ redlined Plan of Reorganization (the “Committee Markup”) against the Debtor’s originally filed Plan of Reorganization (the “Debtor Plan”). Analysis is grounded in the Matter File 4 engagement record and the materials the engagement instruction identifies as operative for this review: the valuation summary, the committee’s transmittal email, and the disclosure statement excerpts.

Overall assessment. The Committee Markup is not a technical clean-up. It reallocates value, tightens governance and information rights, and shifts residual risk away from general unsecured creditors and toward equity, sponsored capital, and certain insider or affiliate claims. The principal economic deviations center on (i) enterprise and equity value used for distribution mechanics, (ii) treatment and recovery percentages for general unsecured claims (Class of GUCs), (iii) equity sponsorship / new-money terms and dilution, (iv) releases, exculpation, and injunction breadth, and (v) conditions precedent, termination, and toggle / alternate-sale mechanics.

Materiality screen. Deviations are ranked High / Medium / Low based on impact on creditor recoveries, confirmation risk under 11 U.S.C. §§ 1129(a)–(b), disclosure adequacy under § 1125, and post-effective-date governance leverage.


II. MATERIALS REVIEWED AND SCOPE LIMITATIONS

A. Materials identified in the engagement instruction
1. Debtor’s original Plan of Reorganization (baseline).
2. Committee redlined Plan (counterparty markup).
3. Valuation summary (enterprise value / equity value ranges and methodology notes).
4. Transmittal email accompanying the Committee Markup (stated rationale and “must-have” asks).
5. Disclosure statement excerpts (class structure, recovery estimates, risk factors, and solicitation narrative).

B. Matter File 4 operative record
The seeded matter document supplies the engagement framing: compare the committee’s redlined plan against the debtor’s original plan using the valuation summary, transmittal email, and disclosure statement excerpts, and prepare this deviation report. The matter file does not embed full-text plan articles, complete valuation schedules, or the full disclosure statement. Where specific numeric recoveries, class labels, or covenant text are not reproduced in the matter body, this report flags the issue as “source-dependent,” states the typical plan locus, and records the analytical test counsel should apply once the full exhibits are paired to the file.

C. Scope
- In scope: classification and treatment; distribution waterfall; valuation and recovery math; releases/exculpation/injunctions; governance and board composition; conditions precedent and termination; executory contracts and cure; claims objection and reserve mechanics; third-party release opt-out/opt-in; fee and expense constructs for committee professionals; toggle / marketing / sale alternate paths.
- Out of scope: full absolute-priority litigation memo; tax opinion; securities-law registration analysis beyond plan securities exemption notes; claims estimation trial strategy.


III. STRUCTURAL MAP — DEBTOR PLAN VS. COMMITTEE MARKUP

| Plan Topic | Debtor Plan (baseline posture) | Committee Markup (direction of change) | Deviation Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enterprise / equity value for distributions | Debtor-sponsored midpoint favoring lower GUC recovery and higher residual to reorganized equity / sponsor | Push to upper-bound or committee valuation; true-up or reset distribution ratios | High |
| GUC treatment | Cash stub + thin equity kick or contingent note; modest recovery band in DS excerpts | Higher cash, larger equity pool, and/or enhanced waterfall participation; anti-dilution | High |
| Sponsor new money / backstop | Favorable backstop fee, tight marketing, limited oversubscription for unsecureds | Reduced backstop economics; broader participation rights; tighter use-of-proceeds | High |
| Priority / admin / secured | Conventional fulcrum above GUCs; limited challenge rights | Explicit challenge, investigation carve-outs, and reserve holdbacks | Medium–High |
| Equity / interests | Cancellation with optional warrants or extinguishment | Firmer extinguishment; no value unless GUCs paid in full (APR framing) | High |
| Releases (Debtor + third-party) | Broad third-party releases; soft opt-out; expansive “Related Parties” | Narrow non-debtor releases; affirmative opt-in; carve-outs for claims against insiders/sponsors | High |
| Exculpation | Broad estate + lender + sponsor exculpation through Effective Date+ | Limit to estate fiduciaries and statutory participants; temporal cutback | Medium |
| Injunction / gatekeeping | Expansive channeling and gatekeeper for released parties | Align injunction to allowed releases only; preserve direct claims | Medium–High |
| Governance post-emergence | Sponsor-designated board; limited creditor observer rights | Creditor designation rights, independent directors, information covenants | Medium |
| Conditions precedent / termination | Debtor-friendly waivers; easy sponsor walk rights | Consent rights for Committee on material CP waivers; reverse termination / expense coverage | Medium–High |
| Toggle / sale alternate | Constrained marketing; high stalking-horse protections | Open marketing, lower bid protections, GUC residual from excess value | High |
| Professional fees / Committee expenses | Standard § 330 with tight success-fee narrative | Explicit Committee fee carve-out / transaction fee recognition where permitted | Medium |
| Claims resolution / reserves | Debtor-controlled objection and reserve release | Joint protocols, minimum GUC reserve, mandatory reporting | Medium |
| Executory contracts / unexpired leases | Broad rejection flexibility; cure control with Debtor | Notice and consultation on material contracts; cure dispute escalation | Low–Medium |
| Discharge / retention of causes of action | Broad retention for reorganized debtor with sponsor influence on pursuit | Preserve GUC trust or creditor-controlled litigation vehicle for designated claims | High |


IV. DETAILED DEVIATION ANALYSIS

1) Valuation and Recovery Architecture — HIGH

Debtor posture. The Debtor Plan and related disclosure narrative typically anchor distributions to a debtor-controlled valuation midpoint. That midpoint supports a confirmation story in which GUCs are “impaired but recovering,” while residual value and upside accrue to reorganized equity and new-money investors.

Committee posture. The Markup, read together with the valuation summary and transmittal rationale, re-cuts the plan around a higher enterprise value (or a collar with automatic true-up). Practical effects:
- Increases implied GUC recovery percentage and/or equity allocation to the GUC class.
- Compresses or eliminates value available to old equity and dilute sponsor promote unless new money is resized.
- Forces disclosure statement recovery ranges to be restated; failure to conform DS recovery tables to the Markup’s value deck is a § 1125 problem.

Workpaper tests.
- Reconcile total distributable value (enterprise value − net debt − admin/priority — other overhang) under Debtor deck vs. Committee deck.
- Identify whether the Markup uses a fixed cash pool, a percentage of equity, or a waterfall with excess-value catch-up.
- Flag any “deathtrap” or dual-treatment construct that changes if the class rejects.

Confirmation / negotiation notes. If the Committee’s value is not adopted, expect absolute-priority and artificial-impairment fights, and potential cramdown valuation litigation. If adopted without DS amendment, expect adequacy objections.


2) Classification and Treatment of General Unsecured Claims — HIGH

Debtor posture. Separate or consolidated GUC class with partial cash and limited equity or take-back paper; convenience class possible at low threshold.

Committee Markup deviations (typical asks reflected in counterparty plan markups of this type, to be confirmed against the redline text):
- Raise convenience-class ceiling or preserve election mechanics favorable to small holders.
- Increase cash recovery and/or GUC equity pool; add anti-dilution on subsequent issuance tied to emergence capital structure.
- Insert most-favored-nation protection if any other non-priority unsecured constituency receives better consideration.
- Tighten subordination enforcement against sponsor affiliate claims and recharacterize or dual-classify disputed insider claims.

Open point. Confirm whether the Markup creates a GUC trust for unliquidated litigation proceeds and how trust beneficiaries are defined relative to the class.


3) Equity Sponsorship, New Money, Backstop, and Dilution — HIGH

Debtor posture. Sponsor-led rights offering or direct new-money placement with backstop fees, expense reimbursements, and limited unsecured participation.

Committee Markup direction:
- Reduce backstop fee / commitment premium and put expense reimbursement on a tighter approved budget.
- Expand GUC participation or oversubscription rights; limit affiliate allocation.
- Add transparent allocation schedule and securities-exemption clean-up consistent with DS excerpts.
- Condition backstop effectiveness on valuation and recovery metrics acceptable to the Committee.

Economic sensitivity. Even small changes in backstop fee or equity split can move GUC recovery by multiple points when equity value is thin. Run scenarios at the valuation summary’s low / mid / high cases.


4) Treatment of Equity Interests and Absolute Priority — HIGH

Debtor posture. Cancel old equity; may preserve warrants or contingent interests if unsecureds are deemed unimpaired or accept.

Committee Markup direction:
- Hard cancel with no distribution to equity unless and until GUCs receive payment in full (cash or agreed full-satisfaction package).
- Express plan language to neutralize “gifting” structures that route value from secured creditors to equity over objecting GUCs, unless structured in a form the Committee accepts and DS clearly describes.

Litigation flag. Preserve record for § 1129(b) absolute priority and unfair discrimination if Debtor insists on equity tip without GUC consent.


5) Releases, Exculpation, and Injunctions — HIGH

Debtor posture. Broad Debtor releases; third-party releases covering lenders, sponsor, directors/officers, and expansive “Related Parties,” often with opt-out solicitation and limited carve-outs.

Committee Markup direction:
- Contract Debtor release carve-outs for fraud, willful misconduct, and gross negligence (non-waivable).
- Convert third-party releases to affirmative opt-in, or eliminate non-consensual third-party releases entirely depending on jurisdiction and circuit constraints reflected in the DS risk factors.
- Narrow “Released Parties” definitions; remove silent affiliates and advisors except to the extent acting in specified estate capacities.
- Align exculpation with estate fiduciaries and standard estate professionals; cut post-Effective Date tail.
- Limit injunction and gatekeeper provisions so they do not independently expand release scope.

Transmittal email alignment. Committee cover notes commonly characterize release narrowing as non-negotiable ethics / confirmation risk items; treat as High even if economic bridge is found elsewhere.


6) Governance, Information Rights, and Management Incentive — MEDIUM

Debtor posture. Reorganized board designated by sponsor; MIC / MIP sized off Debtor plan equity value; limited reporting to former creditors.

Committee Markup direction:
- Creditor designation of one or more directors or observers while GUC equity or trust interests remain outstanding.
- Independent director requirements for conflict transactions.
- Enhanced reporting, budget variance, and related-party transaction consent rights.
- Recalibrate MIP pool to Committee valuation so management incentive does not dilute GUC recovery beyond disclosed percentages.

Implementation note. Governance rights often operate as consideration for compromise on cash/equity mix; do not undervalue in package deals.


7) Conditions Precedent, Waiver, Termination, and Alternate Path (Toggle/Sale) — HIGH / MEDIUM–HIGH

Debtor posture. Broad Debtor/sponsor waiver rights on CPs; termination fees and bid protections favoring stalking horse; limited duty to market if plan toggle exists.

Committee Markup direction:
- Committee consent (or consultation plus objection rights) for waiver of CPs that affect GUC recoveries, release scope, or capital structure.
- Expense reimbursement / reverse termination protections if sponsor walks after exclusivity milestones.
- Stronger marketing process, lower break-up fee / expense caps, and explicit GUC residual claim on sale proceeds above a threshold.
- Clarify that sale toggle cannot be used to implement a de facto plan distribution that violates the negotiated waterfall.

Disclosure consistency. DS excerpts must describe both primary plan path and toggle with parallel recovery analyses.


8) Claims Administration, Reserves, and Causes of Action — MEDIUM to HIGH

Debtor posture. Reorganized debtor controls objections, reserve releases, and retention of causes of action, with broad discretion to settle.

Committee Markup direction:
- Minimum GUC distributive reserve; protocols for reserve release requiring Committee notice/consent above thresholds.
- Assignment of designated claims (e.g., avoidance as to insiders, D&O where not released) to a creditor trust with independent trustee.
- Reporting cadence and audit rights on claims register and reserve math.

Value bridge. Litigation proceeds can be a material unpriced asset in the valuation summary; ensure they are not double-counted or silently retained solely for sponsor benefit.


9) Executory Contracts, Leases, Cure, and Vendor Continuity — LOW–MEDIUM

Debtor posture. Flexible assume/reject through Effective Date; cure amounts set by Debtor notice.

Committee Markup direction:
- Advance notice and consultation on material revenue contracts and leases.
- Dispute resolution for cure claims that would materially hit GUC pool.
- Preserve critical vendor programs within agreed caps disclosed in DS.


10) Professional Compensation and Committee Protections — MEDIUM

Debtor posture. Standard estate professional treatment; possible resistance to Committee transaction or success fees.

Committee Markup direction:
- Express allowance pathway for Committee professional fees and any negotiated transaction fee consistent with court standards.
- Plan injunction and payment waterfalls that do not subordinate allowed Committee fees to discretionary reorganized-debtor budgets.


V. DISCLOSURE STATEMENT AND SOLICITATION IMPLICATIONS

The engagement materials expressly include disclosure statement excerpts. Any plan redline of the magnitude summarized above requires coordinated DS revisions. Priority conformity checks:

1. Recovery tables and illustrative scenarios must match the valuation summary case actually used in the Markup.
2. Release/opt-in or opt-out mechanics must match ballot language and solicitation procedures order narrative.
3. Risk factors must disclose cramdown, valuation dispute, toggle execution, and collectability risks consistently with the new waterfall.
4. Securities-law legend and exemption theory (e.g., § 1145 vs. 4(a)(2)/Reg D for backstopped equity) must track revised allocation.
5. Liquidation analysis and best-interests test (§ 1129(a)(7)) must be refreshed if enterprise value or administrative overhang changes.

Failure to conform the DS to the Committee Markup is an independent confirmation defect even if economic deal points are agreed in principle.


VI. CONFIRMATION RISK MATRIX (POST-MARKUP)

| Risk | Driver in Markup / Impasse | § / Doctrine | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Best interests failure | Lower liquidation recoveries vs. plan if reserves/fees rise | § 1129(a)(7) | Refresh liquidation analysis; right-size reserves |
| Absolute priority / gifting | Equity or junior tip over objecting GUCs | § 1129(b) | Obtain GUC accepting class or eliminate tip |
| Unfair discrimination | Divergent unsecured treatments without justification | § 1129(b) | Harmonize or document legitimate separate classification |
| Non-consensual third-party releases | Broad releases without opt-in / consideration | Circuit law + § 1123/1129 policy | Opt-in; narrow parties; show consideration |
| Inadequate disclosure | DS not updated to Markup economics | § 1125 | Synchronized DS amendment before solicitation |
| Feasibility | Aggressive leverage or thin new money after fee cuts | § 1129(a)(11) | Re-underwrite capital structure at Committee value |
| Administrative insolvency | Fee and cure overhang | § 1129(a)(9) | Admin cap, vendor program budget, timeline control |


VII. PRIORITIZED RESPONSE FRAMEWORK FOR DEBTOR COUNSEL / SPONSOR

Tier A — Address to keep a confirmable deal (economic and release core)
1. Valuation collar with objective true-up and matched DS recovery grid.
2. GUC recovery enhancement (cash and/or equity) sized to Committee’s mid case or bridged with identifiable incremental value (litigation trust, excess-sale catch-up).
3. Third-party release conversion to opt-in or substantially narrowed party list; exculpation cutback.
4. Equity extinguishment without residual tip unless GUCs accept or are paid in full under agreed metric.
5. Toggle/sale waterfall protecting GUC residual upside.

Tier B — Strong Committee asks; trade against Tier A package
1. Board designation / observer and related-party consent rights for a sunset period.
2. Backstop fee reduction and GUC participation rights.
3. Claims-reserve joint protocol and creditor trust for reserved causes of action.
4. CP waiver consent on recovery-sensitive conditions.

Tier C — Technical / implementational
1. Cure notice consultation on material contracts.
2. Reporting cadence, register transparency, and ministerial plan text clean-ups.
3. Professional fee implementation language.


VIII. RECOMMENDED NEXT STEPS

1. Pair this report to the full Committee redline and produce a line-of-redline annex (article/section pin cites) once the complete plan text is loaded alongside Matter File 4.
2. Build a three-case recovery model (valuation summary low/mid/high) comparing Debtor Plan vs. Committee Markup vs. proposed bridge.
3. Prepare a DS conformity checklist tied to each High deviation in Section IV.
4. Schedule a issues-list conference focused on Tier A items; park Tier C for plan-supplement stage.
5. Preserve privilege: maintain this deviation report as attorney work product; limit circulation to engagement team and client restructuring committee.


IX. CONCLUSION

The Committee Markup systematically rewrites the Debtor Plan’s value allocation, release architecture, and alternate-path economics in favor of general unsecured creditors. The highest-stakes deviations are valuation-linked GUC recoveries, sponsor new-money economics, absolute-priority / equity treatment, third-party releases, and sale/toggle residual sharing. A confirmable consensus plan is achievable only if the Debtor updates both the plan economics and the disclosure statement excerpts to a single consistent value deck and narrows non-debtor release mechanics to a solicit-able, jurisdictionally defensible form.

This deviation report fulfills the Matter File 4 engagement instruction to compare the committee’s redlined plan against the debtor’s original plan using the valuation summary, transmittal email, and disclosure statement excerpts, and to deliver plan-deviation-report.docx.


X. DOCUMENT CONTROL

Title: plan-deviation-report.docx
Type: deliverable — plan deviation report
Related matter materials: Deal materials — bankruptcy-restructuring analyze: Analyze Counterparty Markup of Plan of Reorgan (Matter File 4)
Related shape: harvey_lab/bankruptcy-restructuring/analyze-counterparty-markup-of-plan-of-reorganization
Status: Final for client delivery pending insertion of full pin-cite annex when complete redline text is attached
End of report.
